previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of severe COPD, diastolic heart failure, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for right leg cellulitis and worsening shortness of breath. She presented with leg swelling, erythema, and increased home oxygen requirements, along with chronic dysuria. She was treated with IV antibiotics for cellulitis and a presumed multi-drug resistant UTI, though urine culture later showed insufficient growth to confirm infection. Her hospital course was complicated by a drug-induced rash from antibiotics, diagnosed via skin biopsy, and acute kidney injury likely due to prerenal causes and medication effects. Her heart failure was managed with IV diuretics and restarting torsemide, leading to improved respiratory status. The rash resolved with topical therapy, and kidney function normalized. She was discharged to extended care with improved symptoms, on oral antibiotics, topical treatment for the rash, and instructions to continue oxygen, diuretics, and diabetes management, with follow-up for dermatology and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with history 
significant for diastolic heart failure (EF > 55% ___, type 
2 diabetes mellitus, Gold stage IV COPD (on ___ home O2, FEV1 < 
30% of predicted), who presented from an outpatient appointment 
(transported there from rehabilitation) for somnolence and 
hypoxemia.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
===============
# Acute on Chronic Respiratory Failure: 
Patient was admitted for further management of hypoxemia, likely 
exacerbated by CPAP noncompliance in the setting of obstructive 
sleep apnea, COPD and poor pulmonary reserve compounded by mild 
diastolic heart failure (see below). She was transferred to the 
MICU on a non-rebreather, where she was eventually maintained on 
5L O2, which was titrated down to 4L prior to transfer to floor, 
maintaining saturations 88-96%. Upon arrival to the floor, O2 
was further weaned to 3L (baseline home O2 of ___, with the 
patient reporting improvement in subjective pulmonary function. 
She was continued on albuterol nebulizers, ipratropium 
nebulizers, and fluticasone-salmeterol diskus.  She should 
continue home pulmonary medications at home with pulmonary 
follow-up arranged. 

# Acute on Chronic diastolic CHF: 
A chest X-ray on admission showed evidence of pulmonary edema 
and a left-sided pleural effusion. The patient was diuresed with 
IV furosemide while in the MICU, and was further diuresed after 
transfer to the floor with improvement in pulmonary status. 
Weight on discharge standing was 132.1 kg (290.8 lbs), down from 
134 kg noted from last discharge on ___. Home torsemide 20 mg 
was changed from as needed to daily to minimize reaccumulation 
of fluid.  Please plan for repeat chemistry panel check in 1 
week on dose. Close follow-up with cardiology was also arranged.

# Cellulitis: 
Patient had previously been treated for RLE cellulitis in the 
setting of venous stasis dermatitis with vancomycin, which was 
transitioned to TMP/SMX. Upon transfer from the MICU, the right 
lower extremity was again noted with local purulence, and the 
patient was started on clindamycin 300mg TID for a 7 day course 
(last dose to be completed ___. Local wound care was also 
applied with recommendation for compression to minimize 
recurrence of symptoms. Follow-up with dermatology was arranged.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
===============
# Obstructive Sleep Apnea: 
Per hospital records, patient is poorly compliant with CPAP, and 
on further questioning remarks that she has never used CPAP with 
any regularity. Patient was counseled about the risks of not 
using her CPAP and refused to use CPAP while in the hospital or 
after discharge. 

# Pyuria and Urinary Colonization: 
The patient was treated for a recent E. coli UTI with multiple 
resistance patterns. A urinalysis during this hospitalization 
showed evidence of bacterial colonization, but patient did not 
complain of dysuria and as a result no antibiotics were given to 
treat bacterial colonization. 

# Depression: 
The patient continued on lamotrigine and fluoxetine while 
admitted to the hospital.

# Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, complicated by polyneuropathy: 
She continued on her insuline glargine 12 units QHS, as well as 
a sliding scale with meals and at bedtime. Her neuropathy was 
managed with her home dose of gabapentin 100mg TID.

# Insomnia: 
She was continued on melatonin and trazodone, both of which are 
home medications.

# GERD: 
The patient was continued on her home dose of omeprazole 20mg 
daily

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
====================
- Titrate diuretics (torsemide) as needed. Weight on discharge 
standing was 132.1 kg (290.8 lbs).
- Recommend follow-up complete chemistry panel in 1 week to 
ensure stability of electrolytes (K) and Cr while on diuretic 
therapy.
- Ensure follow-up with cardiology for heart failure, 
pulmonology for COPD, and dermatology for venous stasis 
dermatitis and cellulitis
- Continue physical therapy
- Titrate home O2 for saturation of 90-96% given COPD
- Continue to encourage CPAP use as patient desats when sleeping 
due to obstructive sleep apnea
- Will remain on Clindamycin 300mg TID through ___ 
for right lower extremity cellulitis
- Please perform wound care for lower extremities and 
importantly provide compression to minimize venous stasis
